newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude markets steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude markets steady in quiet trade.

text.p: North Sea spot and paper crude markets were steady in quiet trade with benchmark dated Brent and forward spreads rangebound, traders said.
"The market is holding and seems to be rangebound at these levels," a paper trader said.
With the front end of the market in contango, dealers expected to see the overhang of September cargoes continue to disappear despite the tight transatlantic arbitrage window.
Dated Brent was valued steady at Nov paper +12 cents with Oct/Nov paper pegged around +55 cents and the forward spread curve flattening out in a range between +53/+60 cents.
"It beats the cost of storage if you can buy at a contango discount to paper," a trader for a European oil company said.
Traders said improved refinery margins and strong gas oil demand this side of the Atlantic could see sweet grades easily absorbed by refineries replenishing winter stocks.
November Brent paper eased about 25 cents to around $22.05 per barrel in line with weaker IPE Brent futures.
The weaker futures also saw CFD levels for next week's dates slightly softer at Nov +21/+26 cents with Sept 30-Oct 4 dates talked steady at Nov +15/+19 cents.
Two Brent dates are due to turn wet today.
